Transcript Body:
00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the marketplace billing and the connector gate. i'll hand over to maya to run through the spec we sent this morning but first quick intros
00:18 Priya Nair: thanks alex, priya here, we'll be focusing on the listing timeline and the billing side, liam will speak to the platform details, sofia on security and derek on billing mapping
00:34 Maya Patel: great, i'll share my screen, um so the spec is in the partner drive link, note that there's an example webhook and a flattened event format, the fields we've used are fairly minimal - customer_id, usage_id, metric, quantity, timestamp, and an optional tags array
00:52 Derek Wu: quick question, is usage_id the same as our internal invoice key? we generally aggregate by invoice_key across products
01:05 Alex Chen: yep you can map invoice_key to our customer_id or we can accept a usage_id that you map server-side. the important part is a stable key that doesn't change per event
01:26 Liam O'Connor: also what about batching? our system batches events every 5 minutes, we don't want duplication problems
01:38 Maya Patel: we tolerate batching, the schema includes an event_batch_id. we de-dupe by event_id and batch_id, that logic's in the docs. note that sometimes the transcription earlier said 'KV cash' but that was meant to be 'KV cache' in runtime notes, ignore that little typo
02:02 Sofia Alvarez: for the private connector we need mTLS and a KMS-backed key rotation policy. will redwood accept client certs or do you prefer signed JWTs?
02:20 Maya Patel: we support both. for hosted listing the marketplace will have a signed webhook with HMAC secret, for private connectors we recommend mTLS + role-bound certs. we'll need to get your CA chain if using mTLS
02:43 Priya Nair: okay, so marketplace listing requires a public container and a helm chart for marketplace packaging or can we supply an AMI for our bring-your-own infra option?
02:58 Jordan Ruiz: good q. the gate requires at minimum a container image and helm chart. AMI is optional for BYO customers on AWS but good to include. we also prefer a small example deployment that uses our redis/caching pattern so the listing review team can reproduce performance numbers
03:22 Derek Wu: about metering rates — how do we send price tiers? we have volume-based pricing and different price bands per region
03:37 Alex Chen: pricing tiers are captured as part of the billing config in the marketplace listing, but the events only carry the usage quantity and metric name. price calculation is performed when we ingest + map the meter to the configured sku. we'll send mapping guidance in the billing schema doc
03:58 Liam O'Connor: a practical question: what header do you expect to carry the partner id? will it be x-redwood-partner or in the payload?
04:15 Maya Patel: we accept partner_id as an HTTP header x-rd-partner-id and also in payload partner_id field. we try header-first for fast routing
04:30 Sofia Alvarez: about audit logs, we need to confirm what you're storing, retention, and whether logs contain PII. our compliance folks require a SOC2 artifact list
04:45 Alex Chen: absolutely. we keep audit logs for 90 days by default on hosted; for enterprise contracts we can extend retention. we do not retain raw customer PII in meter events — you can hash ids if needed. i'll attach SOC2 scoping docs to the ticket
05:06 Priya Nair: timeline wise we are aiming to have listing review in mid-december, what are the acceptance criteria?
05:18 Jordan Ruiz: acceptance = (1) event ingestion validated with sample data, (2) packaging passes lint + deploy test from our automated checker, (3) security checklist items satisfied (KMS, SSO, audit evidence). we'll document the gate as a short checklist
05:45 Derek Wu: can we run a dry-run where velox sends synthetic traffic and you show how meter aggregation looks in your console?
05:59 Maya Patel: yes, we'll do a runbook test. that will surface any timestamp parsing or duplication issues. recommend a 15 minute spike at 2x peak to validate scaling and metering accuracy
06:18 Liam O'Connor: network wise, private connector will require VPC peering, route table changes, and a tiny NAT. any firewall rules we need to open specifically?
06:32 Alex Chen: outbound to our ingestion IP range on 443, plus port 10250 only for lifecycle hooks if you run the private agent. we'll provide an IP range and CIDR list. note that earlier documentation mis-typed a port as 'ten two five zero' which is 10250, apologies for the fuzzy transcript
06:50 Priya Nair: what about marketplace charges timing and settlement? finance wants to know when the metered events become billable and how refunds/adjustments are handled
07:05 Alex Chen: metered events are considered provisional until we do a nightly reconciliation job. settlement occurs at month-end for most partners, with adjustments allowed via an adjustments API. we'll share the settlement cadence in the billing doc
07:26 Derek Wu: are there rate limits on the webhook? we may have bursts during end-of-month spikes
07:34 Maya Patel: yes, default rate limits are documented; for partners expecting bursts we provide partner-specific quotas. the platform also supports graceful backpressure and can return a 429 with retry-after header
07:50 Sofia Alvarez: SSO integration — will the marketplace control access to the private connector or will velox manage accounts in our IDP?
08:00 Jordan Ruiz: generally the customer controls SSO. Redwood integrates via SAML/OIDC for console access; for connector auth we rely on mTLS or signed tokens. we'll put exact flows in the security playbook
08:20 Priya Nair: any blockers you see from your side for the gate?
08:25 Maya Patel: we need the sample payloads, the helm chart and a basic container image in a registry we can pull from (private registries need a read-only deployment account setup). also want the SOC2 artifact list as noted
08:41 Liam O'Connor: about the example deployment, would you prefer helm values that point to live velox services or to test doubles? we prefer test doubles for initial review
08:52 Alex Chen: start with test doubles, we'll run integration tests against them. once good we flip to staging connectivity to validate real end-to-end
09:05 Derek Wu: security teams will want to review key rotation and HSM usage for KMS — is Redwood's KMS integration through AWS KMS or do you support Bring-Your-Own HSM?
09:20 Maya Patel: we support AWS KMS for hosted, and for private deployments we can integrate with your HSM via standard PKCS#11 or KMIP. we'll include options in the security doc. note: earlier in the transcript 'Redwood Dedicated' was said but sometimes the transcriber wrote 'redwood dedicate' — ignore that
09:41 Priya Nair: competitors — we compared how AstroServe handles billing and they had synchronous pricing attach which caused us problems with reconciliation, curious how you avoid that
09:53 Alex Chen: we intentionally separate usage ingestion from pricing to avoid locking pricing at event time; pricing is a transform during ingestion/aggregation and is stored with a pricing snapshot so you can re-evaluate if price tiers change
10:10 Jordan Ruiz: quick tech detail — aggregation windows can be configured per partner; default is 1 minute but you can increase for lower cardinality workloads
10:25 Liam O'Connor: small nit, what about timezone normalization? all events should be in UTC?
10:31 Maya Patel: yes, UTC recommended. we accept RFC3339 timestamps, will parse and normalize, but please avoid ambiguous local timestamps
10:45 Priya Nair: any docs you can send right now?
10:48 Alex Chen: yes i'll push the billing schema link here: https://drive.redwood.internal/partners/velox/billing-spec (placeholder) and the packaging checklist: https://drive.redwood.internal/partners/velox/packaging-checklist
11:05 Derek Wu: perfect. can we get a short runbook for the synthetic spike test so our ops can follow it?
11:12 Maya Patel: yes we'll provide a runbook with curl examples, k6 load script and expected console screenshots. we'll also include a small script to generate sample events matching your invoice_key format
11:28 Sofia Alvarez: last thing — retention and ability to export raw meter logs for audit purposes, is that possible?
11:36 Alex Chen: yes exports are possible for enterprise customers; we'll include the export SLA in the contract addendum. otherwise you can stream raw events to your S3 via replication connector in private deployments
11:52 Jordan Ruiz: wrap up — next meeting we'll do a short tech validation: v1 billing events exchanged, helm chart deployed to our test cluster, and a security brief covering KMS and SSO. tentative follow-up week of 2026-11-30
12:05 Priya Nair: sounds good, thanks everyone
12:10 Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and owners
